chunks: Truth tables for logic gates. The question: Draw the truth table for NOT/AND/etc gate.
A truth table lists every possible combination of inputs to a gate and the output the gate gives for each one. With 2 inputs there are 4 combinations, so the table has 4 rows.
This question asks you to fill in the table for each standard gate. Once the table is written, nothing about the gate is left to guess.
Think of a multiplication table on a poster. Every possible question is on the edges, and the answer is in the grid. You never calculate, you just look up.
A truth table is the same poster for a gate, small enough to be complete. It is simpler than a times table, because every answer is just 0 or 1.
The same truth table as a waveform. A and B step through 00, 01, 10, 11 (one column each).
Compare AND with NAND, OR with NOR, and XOR with XNOR: in every pair, each bit is flipped.
Notice that XOR is high exactly when A and B differ (columns 2 and 3), and that NOR is high only in the first column.
Row: one input combination and its output, such as A = 1, B = 0 giving Y = 0. Binary counting order: listing rows as 00, 01, 10, 11. It makes a missing row easy to spot.
AND / OR: AND gives 1 only if all inputs are 1. OR gives 1 if at least one input is 1. XOR: gives 1 when the inputs differ. For two inputs that means exactly one is 1.
Complement: swap every 0 and 1. NAND is the complement of AND.
List the four rows 00, 01, 10, 11 for inputs A and B. AND gives 0, 0, 0, 1, because only the last row has both inputs at 1.
XOR gives 0, 1, 1, 0, because the middle two rows differ. NAND is the complement of AND, so it gives 1, 1, 1, 0.
That is the whole idea: list the rows in order, then fill one column per gate.
"With two inputs there are four rows: 00, 01, 10, 11. AND is 0, 0, 0, 1. OR is 0, 1, 1, 1. NAND and NOR are those inverted: 1, 1, 1, 0 and 1, 0, 0, 0.
XOR is 0, 1, 1, 0, high when the inputs differ, and XNOR is 1, 0, 0, 1. NOT just flips its one input.
I remember the rule rather than the columns: AND needs all ones, OR needs any one, XOR needs an odd number of ones. For n inputs the table has 2 to the n rows."
